collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager finds old boundary stones that may change an earlier ruling: the elders look again, or let the neighbors decide.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Last season the elders ruled that the strip of good ground between (subject)'s and (friend)'s gardens belonged to (friend). (subject) accepted it. Now, digging a new bed, (subject) has found a row of old boundary stones under the soil that seem to put the strip on (subject.his/her) side. (subject.He/she) has asked the elders to look again.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The elders come and look. The stones are old, very old, and nobody knows who set them or when. The elders talk for a long time and decide that old stones are evidence, but so is how the ground has been used for years. They split the strip down the middle. Neither (subject) nor (friend) is entirely satisfied. Both of them grow beans on their half.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: The elders ask them to work it out between themselves, with the stones in front of them. They stand over the stones for a long time. At last (friend) says, "What if we just grew something on it together?" They plant a row of melons there. It turns out to be the best row in either garden, which settles nothing, but makes the question seem less important.
